market_question: Will the Republicans win the 2028 US Presidential Election?
reasoning: After two consecutive terms held by a party, the historical win rate for the incumbent party in the next election is about 1 in 4 (25%) since 1960. Adjusting for general uncertainty and the open Republican field without Trump's unique turnout, I estimate the true probability of a Republican win at 32%, below the market's 38.5%.
evidence_points: Since 1960, parties holding the White House for two terms lost the next open election in 3 of 4 cases (1960, 2000, 2016), winning only in 1988.
Absence of Trump on the ballot may reduce the elevated turnout his populist appeal generated, potentially lowering Republican chances.
High baseline uncertainty 3+ years out keeps confidence moderate, but the time-for-change trend supports an edge against the current price.
